title: Licensed Towing & Recovery Operator Directory
demand_signal: Validated by active commercial market plus a structurally captive buyer in motor-club and insurer roadside-assistance networks. Active vendors selling towing/wrecker company lists: BookYourData ('Towing Companies'), InfoGlobalData ('Towing Services Email List'), DataCaptive, LeadsPlease ('Towing & Wrecker Services'), Coldlytics, BlueMailMedia, FrescoData, LakeB2B. The industry has ~75,000 establishments (NAICS 488410 'Motor Vehicle Towing') employing ~140,000 workers and generating $13B+ in annual revenue (IBISWorld 2025). Demand pull is structurally strong because three large buyers MUST continuously recruit towing operators: (1) motor clubs (AAA via regional clubs, Allstate Motor Club, Better World Club, Good Sam, GEICO Mechanical Breakdown, AARP Roadside) recruit independent towers as service providers — every AAA regional club runs an active 'Become an Approved Service Provider' funnel; (2) insurance roadside-assistance third-party networks (Agero, Allstate Roadside Services, Quest Global Services, Nation Safe Drivers, Road America/Cross Country Automotive Services) recruit tow operators to fulfill carrier roadside policies for Geico, Progressive, State Farm, USAA, Liberty Mutual; (3) state DOT 'incident-response' / FSP (Freeway Service Patrol) and police-rotation tow lists in every major metro. All three buyer types pay for clean, jurisdiction-segmented towing-company lists.
target_audience: Motor clubs and roadside-assistance networks (AAA regional clubs — there are 32 in the US; Allstate Motor Club, Better World Club, Good Sam, AARP, GEICO Mechanical Breakdown) recruiting approved service providers — per-truck monthly fees + per-call billing $50-$150 per call; third-party roadside-assistance fulfillment networks (Agero, Allstate Roadside, Quest Global Services/Quest Towing, Nation Safe Drivers, Road America, Urgent.ly, HONK, Cross Country Automotive Services) recruiting tow operators for insurer contracts; towing dispatch and management SaaS (TowBook, Beacon Software/Dispatch Anywhere, Tracker Management Systems/TowManager, Ranger SST, InTow Software) — $100-$1,000/month per company; tow truck OEMs and dealers (Jerr-Dan, Miller Industries Century/Vulcan/Chevron, NRC Industries) — $80K-$300K per heavy wrecker capex; tow truck financing/leasing (PACCAR Financial, Ryder, Penske, dealer floor-plan financiers) — $50K-$250K per truck; auction houses and salvage yards (Copart, IAA/RB Global, ADESA) recruiting tow partners for vehicle pickup contracts — $50-$200 per pickup; impound-management software and municipal-vehicle-storage vendors; commercial auto insurance brokers specializing in tow-operator policies (P&C, garage liability, on-hook coverage) — $5K-$30K/year premiums per company; GPS and ELD fleet-tracking vendors (Samsara, Geotab, Verizon Connect, Motive) — $30-$50/month per truck.
public_data_sources: State DOT / DMV motor carrier registration for towing and wrecker authority (varies by state — some require specific tow-truck operator licensing, others use general commercial-vehicle endorsement)
FMCSA (Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration) Motor Carrier Census for interstate tow operations (USDOT number lookup)
State PUC / Public Service Commission tow tariffs and authorized carrier lists (e.g., CA PUC tow tariff schedules, IL ICC carrier registration)
Municipal police department rotation-tow lists (public per local ordinance / FOIA in most major metros)
State and local nonconsensual-tow regulator registries (TX TDLR Vehicle Storage Facility licenses, FL DACS tow-operator registration where applicable)
City business license registries for towing services
Google Maps / Google Places API (business category 'towing_service')
Better Business Bureau profiles for towing companies
competitive_landscape: Moderately crowded but no jurisdiction-segmented flat-file SKU under $100. The existing vendors (BookYourData, InfoGlobalData, DataCaptive, LeadsPlease) sell broad national towing-company lists at subscription tiers ($800-$3,000/year) or per-contact pricing ($0.15-$0.40), but none cleanly segment by (a) state, (b) heavy-duty vs. light-duty capability, or (c) police-rotation eligibility — the three filters that the highest-LTV buyers (motor clubs, third-party roadside networks, salvage auction houses) actually use when prospecting. DataStructured wedge: $49-$79 per state CSV with three filter fields appended (state, fleet-size-bucket, police-rotation-eligible-flag where city ordinance publishes it). State coverage matches the motor-club and roadside-network buying pattern — Agero buys regional, AAA buys per regional-club territory.
monetization_model: State-level CSVs at $49-$79 each. Fields: company name, owner-of-record, street address, phone, USDOT number (where interstate), MC number (where interstate), state tow authority registration, fleet-size bucket (1-3 trucks / 4-10 / 11-25 / 25+), heavy-duty capability flag, police-rotation participation flag (where city ordinance publishes), 24/7 service flag, years in business (from SoS filing). Top-5 by tow density (TX + CA + FL + GA + IL) bundle at $199. 'Heavy-duty wrecker only' premium SKU at $99 — the smaller-universe but higher-LTV cut for tow-truck OEM (Jerr-Dan, Miller) territorial sales reps.
estimated_market_size: ~75,000 motor vehicle towing establishments (NAICS 488410, US Census 2025). ~140,000 employees. $13B+ industry revenue. Fragmented — top-50 companies account for <10% of revenue (no national consolidator dominates). Buyer LTV: motor club / roadside network per-truck monthly fee $200-$500 plus per-call $50-$150; tow management SaaS = $1.2K-$12K/year per company; tow truck financing = $50K-$250K per unit; salvage-pickup contract = $50K-$200K/year per high-volume operator; commercial tow insurance = $5K-$30K/year premium per company.
data_freshness_requirement: Annual updates with quarterly delta for closures/new entrants. Industry has moderate churn (~10-12% annually) driven by undercapitalization at the small-operator end. FMCSA USDOT census updates daily.
compliance_notes: PASS. State DOT / PUC motor carrier registrations are public record. FMCSA USDOT census is bulk-downloadable public data. Police-rotation lists are public per municipal ordinance / FOIA. City business license registries are public. Google Places business listings are public. No PII — owner-of-record from SoS filings is public corporate record. Source attribution per state DOT/PUC URL and FMCSA URL.
next_steps: Harvest FMCSA Motor Carrier Census filtered for tow operator commodity codes (NMFC towing) to get baseline interstate universe with USDOT/MC numbers
Enrich with Google Places API and Yellow Pages for intrastate-only operators (which FMCSA does not capture)
Cross-reference with state DOT/PUC tow-authority registrations for TX, CA, FL, GA, IL (top-5 by tow density)
Build police-rotation flag from major-metro public rotation lists (LA, Houston, Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta, Miami) — partial coverage acceptable

Launch TX SKU at $49 on Gumroad; outreach via direct LinkedIn to Agero / Allstate Roadside / Quest BD teams, AAA regional-club Approved Service Provider managers, and tow management SaaS partner programs (TowBook, Beacon)
researcher_notes: Strong opportunity because the demand side is structurally captive — Agero, AAA regional clubs, and Allstate Roadside MUST continuously recruit towers (operator churn is ~10-12% annually and policy volume keeps growing), and they explicitly buy state/regional segmented lists. The police-rotation flag is the killer differentiator; rotation-eligible operators are pre-vetted (insurance, licensing, response time) and are a distinct higher-LTV segment that the existing vendors lump into the same generic 'towing companies' bucket. Score 7 (not 8) because police-rotation data is municipally fragmented and requires per-metro FOIA work to fully build — first version ships with partial coverage. Engineering complexity is moderate: FMCSA + Google Places gets ~70% coverage cheap; the last 30% (intrastate-only operators in non-DOT states) needs Yellow Pages and city business license joins. Strong recurring SKU set (50 states + heavy-duty cut + rotation-eligible premium cut).
